predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Fars: 'Ali ibn Buya (Imad al-Dawla) in 934 conquered Fars and made Shiraz his capital'

successors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
successors.text: Fars, the last Buyid seat, to 1062

ledger.x: 934: Ali ibn Buya (Imad al-Dawla) conquers Fars and makes Shiraz his capital.
935: Khuzestan falls to the Buyids.
935: Isfahan, 'the Ziyarid capital', is taken after Mardavij's assassination; the sources say Hasan ibn Buya captured it.
943: Hasan ibn Buya (Rukn al-Dawla) takes Ray and makes it his capital.
ledger.cp: unnamed rulers of the Jibal (page silent)

ledger.x: 945: Ahmad ibn Buya (Mu'izz al-Dawla) takes Baghdad.
967: Kerman is conquered.
972: Oman is largely conquered.
978: Adud al-Dawla marches on Mosul.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 979: the Jazira passes to the Buyids.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 979: the Hamdanids are driven off.
ledger.cpn: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

ledger.x: 980: Tabaristan is conquered.
981: Gurgan is conquered, from the Ziyarid Qabus: 'Gorgan (981)'.
989: Mosul and the Diyar Rabi'a pass to the Uqaylids.
997: Qabus retakes Tabaristan and Gurgan.
1023: Ala al-Dawla becomes a nominal vassal.
1029: the Kakuyid coinage in Majd al-Dawla's name ends.
1029: Mahmud of Ghazni takes Ray.
1041: Kerman passes to the Seljuk Qavurt.
1055: Tughril takes Baghdad.
1062: the Buyid line of Fars ends.

wars.name: Buyid conquest of Baghdad
wars.outcome: Ahmad ibn Buya 'entered Iraq and seized control of Baghdad' in 945 and made it his capital.

wars.name: Buyid civil war of 974-978
wars.outcome: Adud al-Dawla beat Izz al-Dawla at Ahvaz (1 July 977) and at Samarra (29 May 978, Izz al-Dawla having come with the Hamdanid Abu Taghlib), had him executed and held Iraq; in 974-975 he had earlier forced him to abdicate (12 March 975) before Rukn al-Dawla…

wars.name: Buyid-Hamdanid war for Mosul and the Jazira
wars.outcome: Adud al-Dawla took Mosul after the 978 victory, spent a year there and conquered Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar; the Hamdanids briefly retook Mayyafariqin, Abu Taghlib fled to Rahba; the Jazira is dated 979.

wars.name: Buyid conquest of Tabaristan and Gurgan
wars.outcome: Mu'ayyad al-Dawla, helped by Adud al-Dawla, took Tabaristan and Gurgan from Qabus in late 980; Gorgan is dated 981.

wars.name: Buyid-Samanid and Saffarid frontier
wars.outcome: Peace without a border change: in 968 Khalaf ibn Ahmad 'recognized Buyid authority'; in 972 Adud al-Dawla and Rukn al-Dawla paid the Samanids 150,000 dinars after the Baloch campaign that ended on 8 January 972.

wars.name: Uqaylid occupation of Mosul
wars.outcome: The Uqaylids occupied Mosul and the Diyar Rabi'a in 989, forced the Buwayhid governor to flee in 996 and then agreed a treaty that made al-Muqallad 'nominally subservient to the Buwayhids, but in effect he was independent'.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Ray
wars.outcome: Mahmud conquered Ray in March/April 1029 and deposed Majd al-Dawla; Fana-Khusrau failed to restore Buyid power.

wars.name: Seljuk conquest of Baghdad
wars.outcome: Tughril entered Baghdad in 1055 (25 Ramadan 447 AH) and took Malik al-Rahim prisoner; the Buyids of Fars survived to 1062.

certainty.note: Frontiers are approximate throughout: the dynasty was a confederation of three amirates whose borders with the Samanids ('the borders of Khorasan'), Hamdanids and Byzantines (the Syrian front) are not fixed by any treaty on the pages…
